title: pollen
subtitle: the world's radio, carried on the wind, scattered as grains · for monome norns
about: A live granular instrument for the world's radio. pollen tunes into a station somewhere on Earth, catches it on a reel (a loop of the last few seconds, drawn as tape) and scatters it as grains: you choose how far back they reach, how many, how long, how high, and how they're colored. The wind carries you to the next station, near or far, when you drift (K3 on the wind part), or on its own if you give it a pace. Press Start sound and listen.
more: pollen is a script for monome norns, a small computer for making sound. What plays here is the real script, running in your browser: the stations are live, from radio-browser.info (here, only the ones whose servers allow a web page to play them), and the engine is rebuilt in Web Audio with the reverb on the same Mutable Instruments code a norns plays. The screen shows pictures, not numbers.

controls.does: pick a part: wind, catch, scatter, tint, tone or air
shape that part; the two knobs show their names while you turn them
a gesture: drift, press the reel, a burst of grains, play them backwards, static, hold the haze
choose a variety: the wind, the reel's length, the grains' shape, the scale, the media
peek at every part, where its knobs are, and the station
